conviction_note: Small net negative. Growth is weak: Progressive's Q3 letter says the market was 'extremely competitive' and its own new applications fell, and arithmetic on Root's disclosed premiums in force puts Q3 revenue a little under the ~$383M consensus. Against that, losses were benign industry-wide, Root has beaten EPS eight quarters running against a ~$0.61-0.66 bar, and 16.9% of float is short at 10 days to cover. The name has sold its EPS beats on growth (Q2: $1.49 vs ~$0.77, stock -16%), so p_up sits only slightly below 50 (46) and abs_move stays near the option-implied 16.6% (I used 14).
bar: Q3 2026 revenue consensus $382.9M and EPS $0.61 (Benzinga, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/ROOT/earnings-forecasts). EPS $0.66 per Earnings Whispers (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/ROOT). Both are aggregators and do not fully agree on EPS. Root gives no numerical guidance. The only company guide is qualitative: PIF roughly flat with Q2 after quarter end, and full-year 2026 PIF 'relatively flat' year on year if competitive conditions persist (Q2 call, per https://stockunlock.com/investing/root-stock-q2-2026-earnings/). The bar is thin, so every finding is capped small. Q3 2025 comparison: revenue $387.8M, GWP $387M, PIF ~466k, net loss $5M including a $17M Carvana warrant catch-up (https://coverager.com/root-reports-q3-2025-results/).
positioning_check: Short interest 2.08M shares (prior month 2.13M), 16.87% of float, 13.4% of shares outstanding, 10.09 days to cover (stockanalysis.com statistics page read 2026-11-04, https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/root/statistics/). AltIndex had 1.83M and 10.95 days to cover at 2026-09-15 (https://altindex.com/ticker/root/short-interest). Float is 12.3M shares and average volume is ~158k a day, so this is a crowded short. Skew is +0.5 vol points ('balanced'), put/call OI 1.3, total OI only 2,272 contracts, ATM spread 16% of mid. The event-implied move is 16.62% against a historical median absolute reaction of 8.79%, so options price a large move with no direction. Run-up: +15.35% over 20 days and +5.7% over 5 days, with the stock 39% below its 52-week high.

findings.finding: Progressive's Q3 2026 shareholder letter calls the personal-lines market 'extremely competitive'. Market growth 'turned slightly negative', PGR's new business applications fell slightly year on year, and its ad spend rose 18% to $1.6B. Its 10-Q puts personal auto policy life expectancy down 9%, which it attributes to more shopping and competition. Root's Q2 guide of roughly flat PIF (~484k) assumed conditions persist; this says they got harder in Q3, pointing to flat-to-down PIF and new writings on the line Root trades on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-08-05): PIF fell sequentially from 495k to 484k and GWP fell 2% while EPS beat about 2x; the stock fell -16.21% (baseline) on slower growth (https://stockunlock.com/investing/root-stock-q2-2026-earnings/). Q2 2025 also fell -26.37%.
findings.why_not_priced: Root's stock is up 15% in 20 days into the print, which is not the price of a name the market expects to shrink. Root already guided PIF flat, so part of this is inside the guide; what is new is that the industry backdrop worsened after Root last spoke.
findings.independence: PGR's monthly September 2026 release shows personal auto PIF growth slowing to +7.4% from +8.8% in June and NPW +2% in September (https://finviz.com/news/402384/progressive-reports-september-2026-results). Same company, different document. Proxy: macro-to-company transmission that Root has not confirmed.

findings.finding: Progressive's Q3 2026 personal auto combined ratio was 88.7, 'better than target', and its total Q3 CR was 88.7 against 89.5 a year earlier: an industry loss environment that was still benign. Root's H1 2026 favourable prior-year development was $28.5M (vs $14.0M in H1 2025), and Root has beaten EPS eight quarters running. Both make a beat of the ~$0.61-0.66 EPS bar likely (Q3 2025 ex-warrant net income ~ $12M against ~$10M implied by consensus).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS beats have not been paid: Q2 2026 $1.49 vs ~$0.77 consensus, stock -16.21%; Q1 2026 record net income ~$36M, stock +3.38%; Q3 2025 beat, stock -8.79% (baseline moves).
findings.why_not_priced: A consensus at less than half of Q2's $1.49 suggests the street models normalisation (expense ratio back to ~29%, higher loss ratio). A benign peer loss quarter argues the bar is low. But the name's beats are routinely sold, so the reaction is sized small.
findings.independence: Root's own Q2 10-Q shows the H1 2026 favourable development of $28.5M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001788882/000178888226000061/root-20260630.htm). The beat streak is noted at https://www.barchart.com/story/news/3648621/root-s-path-to-profitability-looks-increasingly-linear-if-the-q2-trend-holds.

findings.finding: Root's premiums in force fell to $1,431.7M at 2026-06-30 from $1,472.2M a year earlier, and premium per policy fell to $1,479 from $1,616 while PIF was guided flat. Q3 gross earned premium is then roughly $355-358M. With ceded premium now tiny (Q2 ceded earned $4.6M) and about $26M of fees and investment income, Q3 revenue comes to roughly $375-380M, about 1-2% under the ~$383M consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue $389.2M missed ~$395M consensus by ~1.6%, and the stock fell -16.21% alongside the PIF decline.
findings.why_not_priced: The consensus sits at -1% YoY ($382.9M against $387.8M), as if premium per policy stabilised. Run-rate arithmetic off the in-force book says slightly lower. If priced, the consensus would sit nearer $375-378M. This is my own arithmetic on a disclosed figure, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Shares the Q2 shareholder letter with no other finding. Ceded figures are from the Q2 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001788882/000178888226000061/root-20260630.htm). The revenue consensus is Benzinga's (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/ROOT/earnings-forecasts).

findings.finding: Earnings-quality risk in Root's own Q2 numbers: the gross accident-period loss ratio rose to 61.6% from 57.4% year on year while premium per policy fell 8.5%. The flat 66.0% net loss and LAE ratio was helped by favourable prior-year development of $28.5M in H1 2026, double H1 2025's $14.0M. If releases fade in Q3, the underlying deterioration shows through.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Loss-ratio deterioration was part of the -26.37% reaction in Q2 2025 and the -16.21% in Q2 2026 (baseline). No line-specific reaction is sourced.
findings.why_not_priced: Previews cite the beat streak and the flat combined ratio, not the gap between accident-period and calendar-period loss ratios. The benign Progressive quarter cuts the other way, which is why this is sized small and offset by the second finding.
findings.independence: The accident-period loss ratio is from the Q2 shareholder letter (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001788882/000178888226000060/q22026shareholderletter.htm), the same document as the third finding but a different line.

findings.finding: On 2026-08-31 Root cancelled Carvana's outstanding long-term warrants. It issued a new 1,525,560-share warrant in five tranches at 130-170% of a $55.72 signing VWAP, vesting at 180k-340k new attributed policies and expiring 2028-08-31, and extended the commercial agreement. As of 2026-06-30, $4.3M of the old warrants' compensation cost was unrecognised. A Q3 modification or acceleration charge of up to ~$0.25-0.28 a share in 'other insurance expense' is possible, and the EPS consensus may not model it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 carried a $17M Carvana warrant catch-up that turned net income to a $5M loss; stock -8.79%. Adjusted EBITDA excludes it.
findings.why_not_priced: The 8-K discloses no accounting effect. If the street had modelled a charge, GAAP EPS consensus would sit visibly below an adjusted read. Non-cash and below adjusted EBITDA, so sized at a fraction.
findings.independence: 8-K main document (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1788882/000178888226000068/root-20260831.htm). The $4.3M unrecognised cost is from the Q2 10-Q note (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001788882/000178888226000061/root-20260630.htm). The commercial extension is public (https://www.finanzen.at/nachrichten/aktien/root-extends-embedded-partnership-with-carvana-through-at-least-august-2028-1036514253).

findings.finding: Root has $54M left on a $75M buyback authorised 2026-05-06 ($20.8M used in H1), about 6% of a ~$850M market cap. The stock traded ~$48-52 through August-October (CAO tax withholding at $49.78 on 2026-09-21), so the Q3 release may show meaningful repurchases at levels below today's $55.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: First disclosed in Q2 2026 (>$20M bought); the stock fell -16% on growth regardless.
findings.why_not_priced: Q3 repurchase activity is not public until the release. Inference only: no document shows Q3 buying.

findings.finding: The short is crowded: 2.08M shares short, 16.9% of a 12.3M float, 10.1 days to cover on ~158k shares a day. Thin turnover plus crowded shorts make a squeeze on any upside surprise (an EPS beat, a buyback, a reacceleration plan) a mechanism of its own. The +15% 20-day run-up partly offsets this by raising the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2024 print (2025-02-26) +25.57% (baseline). Prints with large upside moves have occurred on this float.
findings.why_not_priced: The option skew is flat (+0.5), so the market is not paying for an upside squeeze; at the same time, short interest has barely declined (2.13M to 2.08M) despite the run-up.
findings.independence: AltIndex: 1.83M shares, 10.95 days to cover at 2026-09-15 (https://altindex.com/ticker/root/short-interest).

findings.finding: Root said it would launch its newest predictive pricing model state by state in Q4 2026 and that it will 'pursue growth only when it meets our target returns'. The Q3 call is the first update on the rollout and on 2027 growth intent, a possible guidance-line positive against a backdrop where PIF is flat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on a pricing-model launch that I can source.
findings.why_not_priced: Management said there would be little 2026 impact, so the market has not been given a reason to price it. Any 2027 PIF commentary would be new. Sign unknown, sized small.
